name: Kraków John Paul II International Airport
before:
Poland's second busiest airport after Warsaw, at Balice 11 km west of Kraków, handling over 11 million passengers in 2024. That is well beyond the 8 million the current terminal was built for.

The train is the easy way in. The SKA1 suburban line runs from the airport to Kraków Główny in about 17 minutes and continues another 20 minutes to Wieliczka for the salt mine. A roofed footbridge connects the terminal directly to the railway station, a hotel and the multi-storey car park, so a client never has to go outside. Buses run day and night to the main railway and bus stations and the congress centre.

The terminal opened in December 2016, works 24 hours a day and can handle transfer passengers between Schengen and non-Schengen routes in either direction.

The single runway is 2,550 metres.

There is a military area on the south side, home to a Polish Air Force transport wing. The airport is named after Pope John Paul II.
after:
Poland's second busiest airport after Warsaw, at Balice, 11 km west of Kraków. It handles more than 11 million passengers a year.

Trains are the easy way in. The SKA1 line runs from the airport station to Kraków Main Station and on to Wieliczka for the salt mine, and a covered footbridge links the station to the terminal. Buses also run day and night.

Its single runway is 2,550 metres long. The military part of the airport houses the Polish Air Force's 8th Airlift Base. It is named after Pope John Paul II.
